g.text: Both panels are closed-form models, not measured results -- they show the shapes to reason with, not numbers to quote. Left:

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #475569

g.text: pass@k assumes independent samples, so it rises fast, but you only get to keep it if a verifier can tell you which sample was

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #475569

g.text: right. With majority voting instead of a verifier you are capped by how often the modal answer is correct, which is why

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #475569

g.text: verifiable domains behave so differently from open-ended ones. Right: accuracy against thinking tokens is roughly linear in

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #475569

g.text: log compute until it saturates at whatever that problem's ceiling is -- more thinking never rescues a problem the model

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #475569

g.text: cannot do, and wastes tokens on ones it already could.
